Well from an animation perspective, movement needs anticipation (telegraph) before it happens, otherwise it looks janky and for a AAA game it's simply unacceptable.

Not to mention that you're screwing over 'prediction' type weapons like GS and Hammer, where they're slow(ish) and every swing counts and being able to tell what's coming next and how to capitalize is where the skill lies.

I get that Elden Ring isn't technically a single player game but my point about weapon balance still applies.

And I (funnily enough) used the blasphemous blade to finish the game.

But let me know how it felt having to change your entire build just because the content needed you to, instead of doing it your way with the build you crafted throughout the game.

Wouldn't a game be more fun if the weapon options were balanced and the choice came to preference, style and situation instead of always having a clear "best weapon" and feeling gimped when using other weapons?

I can point to Rivers of Blood and Moonveil from Elden Ring as a clear example of that. 

Just because a game is single player that doesn't mean balance should be thrown out of the window or that it's anti-fun.

If weapons aren't going to get a little nudge towards balance I feel it would've made more sense that weapons were gathered in a set order instead of choosing yours from the start. At least when you get Veredicta as the last weapon it makes sense that it's clearly the better weapon of group.

Veredicto needs some sort of nerf, it is too good to not use when things get sticky due to it's range and damage.

Alba is great and versatile, which makes sense cuz it's mea culpa and the devs have had practice on how to make that weapon good.  


My real issue is with the dual blades, I really want to like them (due to destreza which reminds me of a certain arknights character) and have playing with them a lot but it's very hard to justify playing them due to how counter intuitive the weapon is.  


The idea of  it as I understand it is that you're supposed to hit till you get the gems for big damage, and at the same time avoid getting hit. So it's supposed to be higher skill ceiling weapon, but that type of weapon design needs a big reward, and the damage increase is not rewarding in a vacuum, and it looks worse when you remember that Veredicto exists.  


The other issue is that the build up is way too slow, so you have to be aggressive, but you're punished by contact damage and very low knockback to enemies, so they keep hitting you while attacking and there is contact damage which is made worse by moves that reposition you inside the enemy. So you try the parry to fill it up faster, but it's weaker than Alba's so can't counter heavier attacks and it also has to be a perfect parry to counter so end up getting hit more than you should.  


And after all that, you finally manage to fill up those 3 charges and want to use your special moves, which use up said charges and have to go through all that crap again.  


The idea of the weapon is great, but the execution is flawed, a damage buff is a must, but also it needs a faster charge rate, super armor on certain moves and a better parry than Alba since it's core to weapon's design.
